look_here_first: Start with the low soft-looking rosette. Arkansas yucca is a small stemless to nearly stemless species with many narrow flexible leaves, whitish margins that peel into curly fibers, and a comparatively simple flower stalk that is often raceme-like or only sparsely branched.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — current Master Plant Pool Hays-local source flag. Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve flora lists Yucca arkansana. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a dedicated Williamson County treatment.

best_field_traits: leaf margins initially whitish and separating into curly fibers
leaves generally dull green rather than strongly glaucous
inflorescence usually raceme-like or only sparsely branched
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with Y. pallida, Y. arkansana has greener, narrower leaves with obvious curly marginal fibers and a simpler, less-branched inflorescence. Y. pallida is more strongly glaucous blue-green and has yellowish margins without persistent white fibers.
